resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve according to the winner of the special Republican Primary for United States Senator from South Carolina, including any potential runoff.

If no 2026 special South Carolina Republican Senate Primary takes place by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve according to the candidate who is the official Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election.

If the results of the special primary are not definitively known, or if there is no Republican nominee to contest the November 3, 2026 South Carolina U.S. Senate election, by November 2, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be the first announcement of the results from the South Carolina Republican party, however an overwhelming consensus of credible reporting may suffice.

# Research report 1 of 2

As of 2026-08-12, the race is down to a runoff on August 25 between Sen. Darline Graham Nordone and Rep. Ralph Norman. She finished first in the August 11 special primary, with about 32.7% to Norman's 24.6%, but short of the majority needed to win outright. Most of the pages wouldn't load, so many figures below come from search-result summaries.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the South Carolina Republican Party's first announcement of the special GOP primary winner, including any runoff. Credible reporting, such as AP race calls, may also count. I could not open any SCGOP or State Election Commission results page.
- 2026-08-11/12: Unofficial results from WCSC/Live 5: Darline Graham Nordone 32.7% (109,582 votes), Ralph Norman 24.6%, Russell Fry 19.6%, Mark Sanford 14.9%, Mark Lynch 5.9%. Ten candidates ran in total. [Live 5](https://www.live5news.com/2026/08/12/election-results-sc-special-republican-senate-primary/)

## 2. Current status
- 2026-08-11: The AP called it for Graham and Norman, who advance to the runoff. South Carolina requires a runoff when no candidate tops 50%. Turnout was just over 11% of registered voters. [SC Daily Gazette](https://scdailygazette.com/2026/08/11/darline-graham-advances-to-runoff-in-special-gop-primary-its-unclear-who-shell-face/), [Local10/AP](https://www.local10.com/news/politics/2026/08/11/sen-darline-graham-us-rep-ralph-norman-advance-to-gop-runoff-for-us-senate-in-south-carolina/), [NPR/WLRN](https://www.wlrn.org/national-politics/2026-08-11/in-south-carolina-sen-darline-graham-advances-to-a-gop-special-primary-runoff-for-us-senate)
- **Nothing is settled yet.** It is a two-person runoff, and she is ahead going in. Norman edged Fry for second place in a close race.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-11: Graham Nordone and Norman advance to the runoff. Sanford finished fourth. [ABC News 4](https://abcnews4.com/news/local/darline-graham-ralph-norman-advance-in-sc-special-us-senate-primary)
- 2026-08-10: AP preview describes the field as two congressmen (Norman, Fry), former Gov. Mark Sanford and Graham's sister. [Local10/AP](https://www.local10.com/news/politics/2026/08/10/ap-decision-notes-what-to-expect-in-south-carolinas-special-primary-to-replace-sen-lindsey-graham/)
- 2026-07-20/21: She announces she will run for the full term. FITSNews said she had a cool reception from GOP voters and early polls showed her trailing the field. [Deseret](https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/07/21/darline-graham-nordone-announces-she-will-run-for-senate/), [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/20/s-c-succession-drama-darline-graham-nordone-will-seek-full-term-in-u-s-senate/)
- 2026-07-17: Trump endorses her in the special election. Reporting says he recruited her and later campaigned for her. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/17/trump-darline-graham-nordone-senate-endorsement), [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/trump-backs-darline-graham-nordone-primary-replace-lindsey-graham-rcna588075)
- 2026-07-13: Gov. Henry McMaster appoints her as interim senator after Sen. Lindsey Graham died on July 11. [Fox Carolina](https://www.foxcarolina.com/2026/07/13/beautiful-tribute-sc-leaders-react-darline-graham-being-named-interim-senator-after-brothers-death/), [Bloomberg Gov](https://news.bgov.com/bloomberg-government-news/grahams-sister-appointed-to-us-senate-two-days-after-his-death)
- The Democratic nominee is Dr. Annie Andrews, who won the June primary.

## 4. Base rates
- I found no systematic study of South Carolina runoffs. The general pattern in Southern GOP runoffs is that the first-round leader usually, but not always, wins. A Trump endorsement has been a strong predictor in recent GOP primaries.
- Her first-round lead was about 8 points (32.7% vs 24.6%). The combined share of candidates who are now eliminated was about 43%: Fry 19.6%, Sanford 14.9%, Lynch 5.9% and others. I found no endorsements from Fry or Sanford as of 2026-08-12.
- Pre-primary polls were mixed:
  - Trafalgar (Aug 8-10): Graham 26.4, Norman 19.5, Fry 18.4, Sanford 18.3.
  - Emerson: Norman 22, Graham 19.
  - Quantus: Graham 33, Norman 20, Fry 20.
  - co/efficient: Graham 30, Fry 16, Norman 15.
  
  These come from a search summary. [Washington Examiner](https://www.washingtonexaminer.com/?p=4680256), [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/darline-graham-chances-losing-republican-primary-brothers-senate-seat-12304450)
- I found no head-to-head runoff poll dated on or before 2026-08-12.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-07-13: After Trump's recommendation, Kalshi odds that she would be appointed to the seat jumped from 15% to 94.7% within 17 minutes. [Daily Wire](https://www.dailywire.com/news/lindsey-grahams-sister-named-interim-senator-she-accepted-through-tears)
- An aggregator lists Kalshi contracts on the runoff, but the page has no timestamp, so I can't date its prices. [simplefunctions.dev](https://simplefunctions.dev/congress/G000608)
- **I could not find any Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold price for the runoff dated on or before 2026-08-12.**

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- 2026-08-25: The Graham Nordone vs. Norman runoff. Results and an AP call are expected that night. The SCGOP announcement is the resolution source.
- Before then, watch for:
  - endorsements from Fry or Sanford
  - Trump rallies or messaging (he has endorsed her)
  - runoff polling
  - turnout, which was low in the first round at about 11%
- If there were a recount or a dispute, results could be delayed, but the November 2 deadline leaves plenty of time.

# Research report 2 of 2 (written independently)

I could only use material dated on or before 2026-08-12. Most of my searches returned later articles, which I left out. Most page fetches failed because the proxy refused the connection, so many facts below come from search-result summaries and not from the full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question resolves on the South Carolina Republican Party's first announcement of the special primary winner, including any runoff. I could not find or fetch an official SCGOP results page.
- 2026-08-11: In the special Republican primary, Darline Graham (Nordone) finished first with 32.7%, Rep. Ralph Norman second with 24.6%, and Rep. Russell Fry third with about 20%. No one passed 50%, so South Carolina law requires a runoff between the top two. [Roll Call](https://rollcall.com/2026/08/11/darline-graham-will-face-ralph-norman-in-south-carolina-senate-runoff/); [NBC results](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-primary-special-elections/south-carolina-senate-results)
- The runoff between Graham Nordone and Norman is set for Tuesday, 2026-08-25. [Axios, 2026-08-12](https://axios.com/2026/08/12/south-carolina-gop-senate-graham-primary-runoff)

## 2. Current status
- The question is not settled yet. Graham Nordone is in a two-person runoff and finished about 8 points ahead of Norman in round one. Neither of them won a majority, and about 43% of first-round votes went to other candidates, mainly Fry. Where Fry's voters go is the key unknown.
- She is the sitting senator: Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her after her brother, Sen. Lindsey Graham, died on 2026-07-11. [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darline_Graham)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-12: Axios reports the primary is going to a runoff. FITSNews ran a "winners and losers" piece and said Fry's endorsement decision is the next big test. [Axios](https://axios.com/2026/08/12/south-carolina-gop-senate-graham-primary-runoff); [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/08/12/s-c-succession-winners-and-losers-from-the-u-s-senate-primary-election/)
- 2026-08-11: Primary night. Graham Nordone led with about 33% and Norman had about 24-25%. [Roll Call](https://rollcall.com/2026/08/11/darline-graham-will-face-ralph-norman-in-south-carolina-senate-runoff/)
- 2026-07-24: Graham Nordone formally filed to run. [FITSNews](https://www.fitsnews.com/2026/07/24/s-c-succession-darline-graham-nordone-files-to-run-for-u-s-senate/)
- 2026-07-20/21: She announced she would run for the full term. [Time](https://time.com/article/2026/07/20/darline-graham-nordone-lindsey-graham-senate-south-carolina-republican-primary/); [Deseret](https://www.deseret.com/politics/2026/07/21/darline-graham-nordone-announces-she-will-run-for-senate/)
- 2026-07-17: President Trump endorsed her. [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/07/17/trump-darline-graham-nordone-senate-endorsement); [NBC](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2026-election/trump-backs-darline-graham-nordone-primary-replace-lindsey-graham-rcna588075)
- Opponents attacked her over her work at the state Commission for the Blind, including claims that she supported DEI policies. She disputed those claims. The general-election opponent is Democrat Annie Andrews.

## 4. Base rates
- I could not find a systematic study of South Carolina runoffs in the material I reviewed. Two general patterns that may be relevant, but which I did not verify here:
  - First-place finishers in Southern primary runoffs usually win, though not always.
  - Trump-endorsed candidates have a strong record in recent GOP primaries.
- In this race, the leader had only about 33% in round one, which leaves a lot of room for consolidation behind either candidate.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Early July 2026: Polymarket had Fry as the frontrunner at about 60% and Norman at about 18%. [Newsweek](https://www.newsweek.com/lindsey-grahams-senate-replacement-what-the-odds-show-prediction-markets-12189879); [Lower Bucks Times](https://lowerbuckstimes.com/2026/07/14/south-carolina-senate-prediction-markets/)
- Mid/late July 2026: She took the prediction-market lead after Trump endorsed her. [DeFi Rate](https://defirate.com/?p=16519); [Federal News Network](https://federalnewsnetwork.com/prediction-markets/2026/07/odds-south-carolina-republican-senate-special-primary-who-will-replace-lindsay-graham/)
- About 2026-08-07/08, before the primary: Polymarket had Graham Nordone at about 46% and Fry at about 26%. [Newsweek](https://newsweek.com/grahams-chances-of-replacing-brother-on-south-carolina-ballot-after-debate-12280225)
- I could not find a Polymarket or Kalshi price for the runoff dated on or before 2026-08-12. Kalshi has a market on this race. [Kalshi News](https://news.kalshi.com/p/graham-norman-odds-south-carolina-senate-special-primary)
- I found no Manifold market or expert forecast for the runoff dated by the cutoff.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- Endorsements from eliminated candidates, especially Fry, the third-place finisher with about 20%, and from other state Republicans.
- Any runoff debates, new polls and ad spending between 2026-08-12 and 2026-08-25.
- Further campaigning by Trump for Graham Nordone.
- 2026-08-25: Runoff election. After that come the AP call, the SCGOP announcement and certification.
- 2026-11-03: General election against Democrat Annie Andrews. This doesn't matter for resolution unless the nomination is still undecided by then.

- **No runoff data:** no head-to-head poll or runoff market price was available as of 2026-08-12.

**(e) Scenarios**

- **No:** the anti-establishment and anti-dynasty vote consolidates behind Norman. He takes about 60% or more of the Fry, Sanford and Lynch voters who return, her support proves soft in a low-turnout runoff, and he wins about 52 to 48.
- **Yes:** Trump holds a rally or pushes hard on messaging, Fry endorses her or stays neutral, and Fry's voters split evenly or lean her way. She adds enough to her 33% base to win about 53 to 47.

**(f) From base rate to final**

I start at about 67% for a first-round leader. The Trump endorsement and incumbency push up slightly. Her low first-round share as an incumbent and the anti-establishment lean of the eliminated vote push down. A rough transfer estimate (Fry 50/50, Sanford 40/60 to Norman, Lynch 25/75 to Norman) gives her about 51 to 49, which is essentially a narrow edge. Before the primary, Polymarket had her at about 46% in a multi-candidate field; finishing first by 8 points should lift that, but not to a commanding level. I land a little below the base rate.

Probability: 63%
